Code-quality was not adjudicated (no code-quality guide in the repo). 0 deferred; 10 candidates dismissed as noise. All five findings listed here were subsequently fixed on the branch; see code-review-check.json for the per-finding resolution and evidence.

findings.title: Commit subject missing ticket prefix
findings.problem: git-workflow.md requires subjects matching 'EPMCDME-XXXX: Capital sentence'; commit b26eabeb2 is 'support-effort-parameter: add planning artifacts' — a branch-slug prefix with no ticket key and a lowercase first word.
findings.impact: Tekton CI blocks on commit-format violations and AGENTS.md requires the ticket key on every commit, so the branch cannot merge as-is.
findings.recommendation: Reword the subject of b26eabeb2 to 'EPMCDME-13335: Add planning artifacts' (or squash it into an adjacent EPMCDME-13335 commit) before merge.

findings.title: No edit-path test for preserved effort
findings.problem: Regression gap: updateAssistant (src/store/assistants.ts:866-868) now converts a missing effort into explicit effort: null, but no test edits an existing assistant with a saved effort and checks the PUT body still carries it. EditAssistantPage.integration.test.tsx has no effort/temperature/top_p/PUT-body assertions; store tests use hand-built objects only.
findings.impact: Consumers EditAssistantPage.tsx:75 and ChatConfigAssistantForm.tsx:58 both feed form values into updateAssistant; if the edit form stops seeding effort (default-value line dropped, or a mount-time model onChange resets params), every save of an effort assistant clears its effort on the backend and no test fails.
findings.recommendation: In EditAssistantPage.integration.test.tsx, mock GET v1/assistants/<id> returning effort 'high' on an effort-capable model, save without touching Effort, and assert the PUT body carries "effort":"high" (not null).

findings.title: No form test for effort clearing params
findings.problem: Regression gap: on the assistant form, no test checks that picking an effort clears a saved temperature/top_p, or that changing the model clears them, at the request-body level. useModelParamsFields.test.ts only checks mocked clearField callbacks; VirtualAssistantForm tests exercise separate wiring; NewAssistantPage tests never set a temperature before picking an effort or switching models.
findings.impact: AssistantSetupSection is rendered on /assistants/new, the edit route and ChatConfigAssistantForm; if clearTemperature() or resetModelParams() is dropped from its handlers, effort ships alongside stale temperature/top_p (violating the intended mutual exclusivity) and no test fails.
findings.recommendation: Add NewAssistantPage/EditAssistantPage integration tests: set temperature 0.7 and top_p 0.9 on an effort-capable model, pick an effort, save, and assert the body has the effort and no temperature/top_p (null on PUT); separately type a temperature, switch model, save, and assert temperature is absent.

findings.title: Workflow model change not marked dirty
findings.problem: The llm_model_type FieldController now passes onChange={handleModelChange}, which calls setValue('llm_model_type', newModel) without shouldDirty and bypasses FieldController's wrappedOnChange; clearField likewise calls setValue(name, undefined) without shouldDirty. Previously field.onChange marked the form dirty and the workflow validation issue resolved.
findings.impact: Regression: after changing only the model on a workflow assistant node, isDirty() stays false, so WorkflowEditor closes the config panel and ConfigPanel's unsaved-changes guard lets navigation proceed without a prompt — the user's edit is silently lost; the 'model' validation issue is also never marked dirty/resolved.
findings.recommendation: In handleModelChange use the FieldController's field.onChange(newModel) (which marks the form dirty and the workflow issue resolved) or setValue('llm_model_type', newModel, { shouldDirty: true }) plus field.markIssueDirty(); make clearField call setValue(name, undefined, { shouldDirty: true }).

findings.title: Test-coverage acceptance criterion only partly met
findings.problem: The story's testing AC is partial: visualEditorFieldRegistry.test.ts calls registerFields(['effort'], ...) inside the test, so it passes even if 'effort' is removed from VirtualAssistantForm's real registration; VirtualAssistantForm.schema.test.ts covers only effort validation, and no test checks the effort warning in VirtualAssistantForm.
findings.impact: A required story criterion is unmet, and regressions in the workflow form's effort registration or warning would ship undetected.
findings.recommendation: Make visualEditorFieldRegistry.test assert the registration VirtualAssistantForm actually performs (render the form or import its registered field list) instead of calling registerFields(['effort']) itself, and add a VirtualAssistantForm test for the effort token-usage warning.
